mechanism: Daily-reset leveraged and inverse ETFs target a stated multiple of an index's DAILY return. Maintaining that target after the underlying index moves requires portfolio exposure to be reset as NAV and required notional leverage change. The rebalance is therefore a rules-based, recurring demand for underlying/index-linked exposure generated by the product mandate rather than by a discretionary forecast.
claim: The daily leverage-reset mandate creates a causally explicit same-day rebalancing flow whose sign and rough scale can in principle be derived before the close from point-in-time fund assets, leverage target and contemporaneous index move. A later independently authorized test may determine whether a frozen pre-close expression has economic value; no return effect is claimed here.
prediction: Before any outcome access, admissible public documents should establish the daily leverage objective, rebalance/reset convention, eligible instrument mapping and point-in-time fund size. If the sign or scale requires end-of-day holdings published only after the fact, the candidate is not PIT-feasible.
falsification_scope: Mechanism usability is falsified if fund exposures are managed with enough derivatives/internal netting that public AUM and index moves cannot identify executable net rebalance direction or scale point-in-time, or if the expression requires post-close holdings/NAV information. A later negative economic test would falsify only the frozen expression, not the existence of daily-reset products.

decision_map.forced_actor: Sponsors/portfolio managers of daily-reset leveraged and inverse ETFs.
decision_map.constraint: Seek a fixed multiple of the underlying benchmark's daily performance and therefore reset exposure as required by the daily objective.
decision_map.clock: Daily objective measured close-to-close; any admissible expression must be frozen before the relevant close using only information available then.
decision_map.affected_universe: Underlying indexes and liquid futures/swaps/securities used by U.S.-listed daily-reset leveraged/inverse ETFs; later test design must freeze a specific product/index universe.
decision_map.capacity_intuition: Gross AUM times leverage-reset arithmetic overstates market impact when opposing products offset, derivatives transfer risk to counterparties, creations/redemptions change shares, dealers pre-hedge, or underlying liquidity is deep.
implementability_questions: Can point-in-time shares/AUM be reconstructed without post-close leakage?
Can product leverage targets and benchmark mappings be versioned historically?
Can long and inverse products plus creations/redemptions be netted without outcome-dependent inputs?
Can derivatives, spreads, impact and closing-auction costs be frozen ex ante?
active_disconfirmation: SEC investor guidance stresses daily objectives and path dependence but does not imply a tradable price effect.
Fund sponsors can obtain exposure through swaps/futures, transferring or netting hedge demand rather than trading benchmark constituents mechanically at the close.
Long and inverse leveraged products can generate offsetting rebalance needs, and creations/redemptions alter the exposure base.
Sophisticated counterparties can anticipate the reset, so any price pressure may be pre-positioned or competed away.
The mechanism can be real while net market-wide flow is too small, too noisy, or too costly to monetize.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: U.S. SEC Investor Bulletin — Leveraged and Inverse ETFs
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Leveraged and inverse ETFs generally pursue stated multiples of DAILY benchmark performance and reset daily; longer-period performance can differ materially because of compounding.
TQQQ seeks daily investment results, before fees and expenses, corresponding to three times the daily performance of the Nasdaq-100 Index.

legacy_distinctness.screen_scope: Pinned Legacy ledger plus current frozen hypotheses screened before freeze.
nearby_but_distinct: time-series momentum/trend: forecast/factor mechanism rather than product-mandated daily leverage reset
month-end pension rebalance: calendar asset-allocation rebalance rather than daily leverage-target maintenance
Russell reconstitution: benchmark membership replication on scheduled reconstitution dates rather than daily leveraged exposure reset
0DTE dealer gamma: option inventory hedging rather than ETF leverage mandate

next_validator_decision.PASS_TO_TEST_DESIGN: A fully PIT product/AUM/benchmark mapping and pre-close reset expression can be frozen without post-close holdings or returns.
next_validator_decision.PARK_DATA: Mechanism is documented but historical PIT AUM/creation-redemption or exposure mapping cannot be reconstructed cleanly.
next_validator_decision.KILL_MECHANISM: Public information cannot identify net rebalance exposure sufficiently before the close or the proposed expression necessarily uses outcome-dependent inputs.
